title: Head lift, stopping, riding, poking
summary: Four common causes of misses, head lift, stopping or checking the gun, riding the target and poking, with what each looks like and the usual cure.

body.html: After the direction, the coach names the cause. Four causes come up in most training sessions, each with its own short word. Learn them in pairs: the fault and the cure.

Head lift: the cheek leaves the stock at or just before the shot, often because the shooter wants to see the clay break. Your eye does the job of a rear sight (a shotgun has none). So when the head comes up, the eye moves, the gun points higher than you think, and the shot usually goes over the top. Cure: 'head down', 'cheek on the stock', 'stay in the gun'.

Stopping the gun: the barrels stop at the shot, usually because the shooter glances at the barrel to check the gap in front of the target. The shot goes behind. A lighter version is checking: the swing hesitates for a split second. Cure: 'keep the gun moving', 'follow through', 'finish the shot'.

Riding the target: following the clay too long before firing, so it slows, drops or curls away and the shooter loses the line. Cure: 'take it earlier', 'commit to it'. Poking (also 'aiming', 'measuring'): pointing the shotgun slowly like a rifle, eyes on the bead (the small dot at the end of the barrels) instead of the clay. It is typical when the break point is too close, or on a teal (a target thrown almost straight up) at the top of its climb. Cure: 'eyes on the clay', 'let the gun go'.

A related fault is the flinch: an involuntary jerk just before the shot, often from expecting the recoil. A gun that fits, lighter cartridges and work with a coach usually help; see Recoil, shoulder and neck.

notes.html: Coaches often name the cause before the shooter has even lowered the gun. Translate it in the same breath and with the same verb: 'you stopped' is not 'you missed'. A word like 'aiming' is almost always a criticism, so avoid turning it into advice such as 'aim better'.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You lifted your head, that's why it went over.
phrases.meaning: The cheek left the stock, so the shot went above the clay.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Keep the gun moving, you stopped on it.
phrases.meaning: The swing halted at the shot; continue moving through and after it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You checked just before the shot, commit to it.
phrases.meaning: A brief hesitation before firing; decide and shoot without slowing.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Stop aiming, look at the bird and let the gun go.
phrases.meaning: Criticism: the shooter is pointing like a rifle; focus on the target and swing freely.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You rode it too long, take it earlier.
phrases.meaning: The shooter followed the clay too long; break it sooner.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.meaning: Keep the cheek on the stock until after the shot.

key_points.html: Head lift: shot usually over; cure: head down, stay in the gun.
Stopping or checking: shot behind; cure: keep the gun moving, follow through.
Riding: the clay slows or drops away; cure: take it earlier, commit.
Poking or aiming: slow rifle-like pointing; cure: eyes on the clay.
Flinch: a jerk before the shot, often from recoil; check gun fit and cartridges.

quiz.q: The coach says 'You lifted your head'. Where did the shot most likely go?
quiz.explain: Your eye does the job of a rear sight (a shotgun has none): when the head lifts, the shot usually goes over.

quiz.q: A coach shouts 'Stop aiming!'. What does he want?

options.text: Don't point like a rifle: look at the target and swing
Aim more carefully along the rib at the clay
Stop shooting and open the gun at once
Lower the gun and wait for the referee

quiz.explain: 'Aiming' in a coach's mouth is a fault (poking); the cure is eyes on the clay and a free swing.

options.text: The trap threw the target too slowly
The shooter started too far behind
The shooter followed the clay too long

quiz.explain: Riding the target means following it too long, so it slows or drops and the line is lost.
